title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Over a smooth curve X/S (relative dimension 1, ω = Ω^1_{X/S} invertible) there is a P^1-bundle P → X with a section σ. Equivalently there is a locally free V of rank 3 with a filtration Ω = Fil_1 V ⊂ L ⊂ V. Here Ω ≅ σ^*(Ω^1_{P/X}), and L is the rank-2 piece; the next page gives 0 → ω → L → O_X → 0. This is essentially the adjoint (or conic) model of a PGL_2-bundle with a reduction to the Borel subgroup.

Previous page. For a connection c on V, the second-fundamental-form component c_{2,3}: Ω → ω (Kodaira–Spencer type) is considered. c is called 'transverse' (nowhere stationary) when c_{2,3} is an isomorphism. One fixes an isomorphism i: Ω ≅ ω and restricts to connections with c_{2,3} = i. These form a torsor under L⊗ω. In modern terms these are PGL_2-opers, i.e. Gunning's indigenous bundles.

This page.
1. The restriction c|Ω: Ω → L⊗ω is a differential operator of order ≤ 1. Hence it factors as Ω --d^1--> P^1_{X/S}(Ω) --γ--> L⊗ω, with d^1 the universal first-order operator and γ O_X-linear.
2. The composite Ω → L⊗ω → (L/Ω)⊗ω = ω is O_X-linear, equal to −2i. The factor −2 presumably comes from the bracket or quadratic-form normalisation on the rank-3 bundle. So γ is a morphism of extensions:
   - top row: 0 → Ω⊗ω → P^1(Ω) → Ω → 0;
   - bottom row: 0 → Ω⊗ω → L⊗ω → ω → 0;
   - with γ_0 on the kernels and −2i on the quotients.
3. Computing γ_0. In P^1, ω_1⊗df corresponds to d^1(fω_1) − f d^1(ω_1). So γ(ω_1⊗df) = c(fω_1) − f c(ω_1). Write ω_1 = λδ; by Leibniz this equals δ⊗[d(fλ) − f dλ] = λδ⊗df. Hence γ_0 = Id: the symbol of a connection is the identity.
4. Conclusion (remark). If c is transverse and 2 is invertible, the five lemma makes γ an isomorphism of extensions, inducing Id on the kernels and −2i on the quotients.

Next page. This yields L ≅ P^1_{X/S}(ω)⊗ω^{-1}. The extension class of L (of O_X by ω) is −2 times the canonical principal-parts (Atiyah-type) class of ω. Equivalently, after rescaling by −1/2, the restriction of c to Fil_1 becomes the universal operator d^1_ω. The remaining freedom in the transverse connection is then a section of ω^{⊗2}, i.e. the quadratic-differential (projective-structure / Schwarzian) torsor.

Purpose. This is part of setting up the general theory of transverse connections on P^1-bundles (projective structures, uniformising indigenous bundles). It sits in a dossier on Gauss–Manin connections for families of elliptic curves, where Kodaira–Spencer gives transversality, and on Picard–Fuchs equations and the Cartier operator.
errors: No substantive error. The constant −2 on the quotient is imported from a previous computation not fully visible here; it is convention-dependent (normalisation of the bracket or quadratic form on V). The line 'Donc' right after γ_0 = Id is left unfinished; the conclusion is moved into the Remarque. The iso claim needs 2 invertible, which is correctly stated.

ideas.what: Restriction of a connection to the first Hodge/Borel step is a first-order differential operator, so it factors through principal parts P^1(Ω) via an O-linear map γ whose symbol γ_0 is the identity.
ideas.modern_name: Symbol of a connection / factorisation through jet bundles (EGA IV §16 principal parts)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (EGA IV 16) for the formalism; standard

ideas.what: For a transverse connection on a P^1-bundle with section (rank-3 filtered bundle), with 2 invertible, the middle filtration step L is canonically isomorphic to P^1(ω)⊗ω^{-1}. Its extension class is −2 times the principal-parts class of ω.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical form / Hodge-filtered bundle of a PGL_2-oper (indigenous bundle); jet-bundle description of opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967, indigenous bundles); Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Mochizuki (1996, indigenous bundles in mixed/positive characteristic)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; possibly related to unpublished material on Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs

ideas.what: Transverse connections with fixed Kodaira–Spencer iso form a torsor; after normalising c|Ω = d^1_ω, the remaining freedom is a section of ω^{⊗2}.
ideas.modern_name: Affine space of projective structures / opers modelled on quadratic differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarzian derivative); Gunning; Beilinson–Drinfeld; Mochizuki in arithmetic setting

missed.claim: Around 1972 Grothendieck developed, over a general base S and characteristic ≠ 2, the scheme-theoretic theory of 'transverse' (nowhere stationary) connections on P^1-bundles with section. He works with PGL_2 / rank-3 bundles, without square roots of ω. This yields the canonical identification L ≅ P^1(ω)⊗ω^{-1} with the factor −2. Arithmetically this is the indigenous-bundle formalism later central to Mochizuki's p-adic Teichmüller theory, which is not attributed to Grothendieck. It is an unpublished early instance rather than a new result.
missed.quote: Si c connexion transversale, et 2 inversible sur X, alors γ est un iso d'extensions de P^1_{X/S}(Ω) et L⊗ω
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context. It links Gauss–Manin/Kodaira–Spencer on modular curves, Cartier operator and p-curvature (same dossier) with indigenous bundles years before Mochizuki's dormant/ordinary indigenous bundles.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a routine local computation leading to a known structural fact about opers/indigenous bundles. The interest is historical: an early, general-base, square-root-free treatment of transverse connections by Grothendieck in a Gauss–Manin / Cartier-operator context.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'On sait que le composé avec / L⊗ω → ω / est −2i' rather than 'On sait que on a aussi ... → −2iω'.
Under the first arrow: 'op. diff. canon. d'ordre 1' (universal differential operator d^1) rather than 'op. diff. com'; under γ: 'lin.' (linéaire).
The composite map is labelled c|Ω (restriction of c to Ω), not c(ω)/c(Ω).
'quitte à supposer [?] soit section δ_0 de Ω' probably 'quitte à supposer que Ω admette une section (base) δ_0'.
Right end of second-to-last line: 'et 2 inv. sur X' added above the Remarque.
